precepts.text: Fear not, thou worm Jacob; I will help thee, saith the Lord and thy redeemer.
precepts.point: The Lord is a man of war. War is coming to this place, and through those wars Israel's salvation comes.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

precepts.text: But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen.
precepts.point: The ten pounds are money in the parable, but they stand for the word of God, the commandments. Occupy till I come.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.text: Israel is the servant, Jacob the chosen, the seed of Abraham; Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham.
precepts.point: The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
The covenant is “between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant.” Seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor, and Isaiah names that seed: “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.”

Israel is the servant, Jacob the chosen, the seed of Abraham. Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham, and the Most High promised “to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.” That is the God of Israel.

precepts.text: But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend; I have taken thee from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.
precepts.point: No other nation can lay claim to this: our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and the Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. Heavy scriptures right there.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” The heaven and the heaven of heavens are the Lord's, the earth also, with all that therein is; and out of all of it, “Only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people”. Our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and Israel is the seed of that friend, chosen because the Lord delighted in the fathers.

“Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” The Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. No other nation can lay claim to this. And he has not cast us away; the choosing stands “as it is this day.” Heavy scriptures right there.

precepts.text: The precept that God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, the seed of Abraham.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, for I am with thee; I will strengthen thee and uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness. All that were incensed against Israel shall be ashamed and confounded, be as nothing, and perish; those that war against Israel shall be as a thing of naught.

note.label: Isaiah 41: Israel My Servant, the Chosen Seed

precepts.why:
“But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend”, and “I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” Paul asks and answers the same thing: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

God has not cast away his people, the seed of Abraham, and Paul proves it by himself: an Israelite, of the tribe of Benjamin. When the New Testament speaks of the chosen and the servants, it is talking about Israel; the servants of God are Israelites and the chosen of God are Israelites, all twelve tribes, not everybody. The Most High took Israel from the ends of the earth and said, “Thou art my servant”, and he holds Israel’s right hand, saying, “Fear not; I will help thee.”

precepts.text: Israel is the Lord's servant, Jacob whom He chose, the seed of Abraham, taken from the ends of the earth; it is not all people.
precepts.point: The Most High never comes down here Himself to speak to the people; He speaks through His servants the prophets.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

precepts.why:
The servants the Lord sends are taken out of one people: “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” Israel is the Lord's servant, Jacob whom he chose, the seed of Abraham. It is not all people.

“Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” The prophets that rose up early to warn Judah were of this servant, and so are the ones teaching on the corners today. Even after the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and being driven among all the nations, Israel is chosen and not cast away.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 22

precepts.why: For the many who say the Bible is not faithful and true, this is what you say to the scoffer: “Produce your cause, saith the Lord; bring forth your strong reasons.” “Let them bring them forth, and shew us what shall happen”: show us in ancient writings why we went into slavery on ships, what will happen to America, Syria, Egypt. Islam, Christianity, the Gilgamesh epic, the Quran, the books of Buddha and Krishna can’t do it; only the Bible can. “Let them shew the former things, what they be, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them.” “Shew the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods”: some say the black man is God; then why did God go into slavery? “Behold, ye are of nothing, and your work of nought: an abomination is he that chooseth you”: anyone who chooses Islam or Christianity is an abomination.
